name: test

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.23"
      - name: build
        run: go build ./...
      - name: vet
        run: go vet ./...
      - name: gofmt
        run: test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"
      - name: test
        run: go test ./...

name: release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*.*.*"]
  release:
    types: [published]

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: install build deps
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y cmake build-essential
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.23"
      - name: cache native build
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: third_party
          key: native-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('Makefile') }}
      - name: build static binary
        run: make release-bin
      - name: resolve tag and asset name
        id: meta
        run: |
          TAG="${{ github.event.release.tag_name || github.ref_name }}"
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "asset=voicekbd-$TAG-linux-x86_64" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: name the artifact
        run: cp bin/voicekbd "${{ steps.meta.outputs.asset }}"
      - name: create release if missing
        run: |
          gh release view "${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || gh release create "${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}" --generate-notes
      - name: upload artifact and license files (idempotent)
        run: |
          gh release upload "${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}" \
            "${{ steps.meta.outputs.asset }}" \
            LICENSE \
            THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES \
            --clobber

# Voice Keyboard A system-wide voice dictation tool for Wayland that behaves like a keyboard. Press a key, speak, and the transcribed text is typed into whatever window has focus, the way the microphone button on a phone keyboard works, but for any desktop text input. Everything runs locally. Audio is transcribed on your machine and never leaves it.

## Features - **Types into any focused window** via `wtype` (the virtual-keyboard Wayland protocol), so it works in terminals, browsers, editors, GTK and Qt apps. - **Two ways to talk:** - **Toggle** - press once to start listening, pause (silence auto-stop) or press again to finish. - **Push-to-talk** - hold a key while you speak, release to inject. No silence detection, so a mid-sentence pause never cuts you off. With the streaming model, text is typed incrementally while you hold the key; releasing drains the remaining audio and finalizes the last words. - **Warm daemon** - the speech model loads once and stays resident, so there is no multi-second delay on each activation. - **Tray indicator** - an icon shows the state at a glance: gray when idle, red while listening, amber while transcribing, dimmed when the daemon is not running. Its "Open Settings" menu item opens a local settings page in your browser. - **Configurable** via a small TOML file (model path, language, streaming on/off, listening and silence tuning, trailing space) or the settings GUI. - **Private** - local-only transcription, no network, and the microphone is open only while you are actively dictating. ## How it works ``` sway keybind --exec--> voicekbd toggle --> unix socket --> voicekbd daemon | model warm in RAM mic capture --> VAD --> parakeet STT --> wtype --> focused app | in-process tray (--tray) status icon ``` Speech-to-text uses [mudler/parakeet.cpp](https://github.com/mudler/parakeet.cpp) (the multilingual streaming `nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b` model) through cgo, kept warm inside a long-running daemon. A sway keybind runs `voicekbd ` (for example `voicekbd toggle`), which sends one-word commands over a Unix socket in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. Starting the daemon with `voicekbd --tray` also shows a status tray icon in the same process. ## Requirements - A wlroots-based Wayland compositor (developed on **sway**). - **`wtype`** (`pacman -S wtype` on Arch) for text injection. - A working microphone (captured through PipeWire or ALSA). - For the tray icon: a StatusNotifierItem host, such as **waybar's `tray` module** (also KDE, or GNOME with the AppIndicator extension). - To build: **Go 1.23+**, **cmake**, and a **C++ toolchain** (the speech library is compiled from source). ## Install (release binary) Download the latest `voicekbd-vX.Y.Z-linux-x86_64` from the [Releases](https://github.com/jimmykarily/voice-keyboard/releases) page, then: ```sh chmod +x voicekbd-*-linux-x86_64 mv voicekbd-*-linux-x86_64 voicekbd ./voicekbd --fetch-model # downloads the default speech model (about 1.4 GB) ./voicekbd --tray # start the daemon with a status tray icon ``` The binary is self-contained (no separate libraries to install). It still needs `wtype` for text injection and a StatusNotifierItem host for the tray icon (see Requirements above). ### Getting the model manually `--fetch-model` downloads the default model for you. To do it by hand instead: ```sh curl -L --create-dirs \ -o ~/.local/share/localai/models/parakeet-cpp/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b-f16.gguf \ 'https://huggingface.co/mudler/parakeet-cpp-gguf/resolve/main/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b-f16.gguf?download=true' ``` ### Where models live voicekbd stores models under `~/.local/share/localai/models/parakeet-cpp/`, the same directory [LocalAI](https://localai.io) uses. This is deliberate: if you already run LocalAI, the models are shared instead of duplicated. ## Build Building from source instead of using a release binary also works, and is required if you want to modify the code. The native speech library and the model are produced by `make` targets and are not committed to the repository. ```sh make lib # build libparakeet.so from source (one-time, cached; needs cmake + C++) make model # download the multilingual streaming GGUF model into ~/.local/share/localai/models/parakeet-cpp/ make build # build the single bin/voicekbd ``` `make lib` clones and compiles `mudler/parakeet.cpp` into `third_party/`; it is idempotent, so later builds reuse the cached library. `bin/voicekbd` is linked against that library with an absolute rpath, so it runs without any `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Because that rpath is absolute, the binary is not relocatable: if you move the checkout, re-run `make build`. To sanity-check the speech path end to end (punctuation and capitalization survive), run `make smoke`. ## Run Get the exact config lines for your checkout: ```sh make sway-help ``` It prints the lines to add to `~/.config/sway/config`. They look like this (with absolute paths filled in): ``` # Start the warm daemon with a status tray icon (sway exec gives it the session env wtype needs) exec /path/to/voice-keyboard/bin/voicekbd --tray # Toggle dictation bindsym $mod+Shift+v exec /path/to/voice-keyboard/bin/voicekbd toggle # OR push-to-talk: hold to talk, release to inject bindsym --no-repeat $mod+v exec /path/to/voice-keyboard/bin/voicekbd start bindsym --release $mod+v exec /path/to/voice-keyboard/bin/voicekbd stop ``` Reload sway (`$mod+Shift+c`). Then focus a text field, trigger dictation, and speak. You can bind both toggle and push-to-talk to different keys. Launching the daemon from `sway exec` (rather than a systemd service) is deliberate: it inherits the Wayland session environment that `wtype` needs to reach the compositor. ### Controlling the daemon `voicekbd ` talks to the running daemon: ```sh voicekbd status # idle | listening | transcribing voicekbd toggle # toggle-mode dictation voicekbd start # begin push-to-talk recording voicekbd stop # end push-to-talk recording and inject voicekbd subscribe # live state stream (handy for debugging) voicekbd quit # stop the daemon ``` ## Configuration All settings live in `~/.config/voicekbd/config.toml`. Without it, the daemon uses built-in defaults. Write a commented starting point: ```sh voicekbd --write-config ``` The daemon reads the config once at startup, so restart it after editing. Defaults: ```toml [engine] model_path = "~/.local/share/localai/models/parakeet-cpp/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b-f16.gguf" target_lang = "auto" # locale prompt for the multilingual model, e.g. "en", "es" streaming = true # incremental push-to-talk typing; false reverts to batch [audio] silence_sec = 0.7 # trailing silence that ends a toggle utterance min_speech_sec = 0.1 # reject sub-100ms blips max_utterance_sec = 20.0 # hard cap (also the push-to-talk safety cap) calibration_sec = 0.3 # ambient-noise calibration window threshold = 0.0 # 0 = auto-calibrate to ambient noise max_threshold = 0.05 # ceiling on the auto-calibrated threshold [inject] backend = "wtype" # only wtype is implemented today trailing_space = true ``` The model is downloaded into a shared LocalAI directory (not duplicated) via `make model`. The download is skipped if the file already exists. Set `model_path` to override the location. With `streaming = true` (the default), holding the push-to-talk key feeds audio to the model continuously and types each recognized chunk as it arrives; releasing the key drains any remaining audio and finalizes the last words. Set `streaming = false` to fall back to the older batch behavior, where nothing is typed until the key is released. `target_lang` selects the language the multilingual model expects (`"auto"` to let it detect the language, or a code such as `"en"`/`"es"` to pin it). Toggle mode is unaffected by `streaming` and always transcribes in a single batch on silence or the second press. The `[audio]` knobs tune the voice-activity detection used in toggle mode (they have no effect in push-to-talk, which stops on key release). Useful flags: `voicekbd --config `, `voicekbd --socket `, and `voicekbd --oneshot` (capture one utterance, transcribe, inject, then exit; a debug aid). ### Settings GUI The daemon serves a settings page you can open from the tray icon's "Open Settings" item. It opens in your default browser, edits every setting in `config.toml`, and can download and switch speech models without leaving the page. The page is only reachable from this machine: the daemon binds it to a random port on `127.0.0.1` and generates a one-time session token when it starts, and both the page URL and every API request carry that token. There is no password and no separate login; anyone with a shell on the machine while the daemon is running can already read `config.toml`, so the token exists to keep the page from being reachable over the network, not to add a new trust boundary. Saving from the page applies the new settings to the running daemon immediately, as long as it is idle (not currently listening or transcribing); if you save while dictating, the daemon keeps its current settings and the page reports that the change did not apply, so you can try again once you are idle. The saved file is written either way and takes effect on the next successful save or daemon restart. Editing `config.toml` by hand still works exactly as before; a manually edited file takes effect after either a daemon restart or the next Save from the settings page. ## Privacy - Transcription is fully local. Nothing is sent over the network and there is no telemetry. - The microphone is opened only between activation and the end of an utterance. It is closed while idle and while transcribing. - Audio is processed in memory and is not written to disk. ## Troubleshooting - **Nothing gets typed.** Confirm `wtype` is installed and you are in a Wayland session (`echo $XDG_SESSION_TYPE` should print `wayland`). The daemon must run with the session environment, which `sway exec` provides. - **Toggle mode does not stop when I pause.** Push-to-talk avoids silence detection entirely and is the most reliable mode. Otherwise tune the `[audio]` knobs (a quieter mic may need a lower `max_threshold`). - **The tray icon does not appear.** You need a StatusNotifierItem host, for example waybar's `tray` module. - **`voicekbd status` says the daemon is not running.** Start `bin/voicekbd` (it is the `exec` line from `make sway-help`). ## Credits This project stands on the work of others. - **[Ettore Di Giacinto (mudler)](https://github.com/mudler) and the [parakeet.cpp](https://github.com/mudler/parakeet.cpp) contributors.** parakeet.cpp is the tool that triggered the idea behind this voice keyboard, and it is the speech-to-text engine at its core. It is brought to you by the [LocalAI](https://localai.io) team, whose model directory voicekbd reuses so models are shared rather than duplicated. - **[Georgi Gerganov](https://github.com/ggerganov) and the [ggml](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml) project.** parakeet.cpp is built on ggml, which runs the model on your machine. Local-only transcription is possible because of it. - **The [NVIDIA NeMo](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/NeMo) team.** The Parakeet and `nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b` speech-recognition models are their work; parakeet.cpp is an inference port of them. - **The [wtype](https://github.com/atx/wtype) project.** The Wayland virtual-keyboard injection is what lets transcribed text land in whatever window has focus, which is what makes this a keyboard at all. Voicekbd also leans on several Go libraries for audio capture, the tray icon, and config parsing (`malgo`, `fyne.io/systray`, `BurntSushi/toml`, and the `go-audio` packages). Thanks to their authors too. ## License Voicekbd is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). It links against [parakeet.cpp](https://github.com/mudler/parakeet.cpp) and [ggml](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml), both also MIT. The other bundled dependencies are all permissive (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, and public domain). Their full license texts are reproduced in [THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES](THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES). The speech model weights are a separate matter: they are governed by NVIDIA's model licenses (for example the multilingual `nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b` is under OpenMDW-1.1), not by this project's license. Check the model card on Hugging Face before redistributing weights. ## Status and design This implements local dictation: speech to text injected as keystrokes. Push-to-talk streams and types incrementally as you hold the key, using the multilingual `nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b` model; toggle mode still runs a single batch transcription on silence or the second press. This project is developed with heavy use of AI tools.
